title: Translate approved shopping-plan lines into Instacart products_link line items
body:
## Role
A backend engineer who owns a lossy translation and makes every loss visible.

## Goal
Translate approved shopping-plan lines into documented `products_link` line items, preserving intent and refusing to guess.

## Context
Field rules from the [official docs](https://docs.instacart.com/developer_platform_api/api/products/create_shopping_list_page):
- `name` is required and is the search term; `display_text` overrides what the user sees.
- Prefer `line_item_measurements` (top-level `quantity`/`unit` are marked deprecated). An unsupported unit makes quantity matching fail.
- `upcs` (12 or 14 digits) and `product_ids` are mutually exclusive, and duplicates across lines are a 400.
- `filters` are ignored whenever UPCs or product IDs are present.
- `health_filters` is a closed set (ORGANIC, GLUTEN_FREE, FAT_FREE, VEGAN, KOSHER, SUGAR_FREE, LOW_FAT); `brand_filters` are case-sensitive catalog spellings.
Hard constraints come from #145.

## Deliverables
- `fulfillment/instacart/translate.py`: `translate(plan) -> TranslationResult(request, issues)`.
- A unit map from Grocery Butler units to supported Instacart units, built from the official units page.
- `TranslationIssue` kinds: `unsupported_unit`, `ambiguous_mapping`, `hard_constraint_unrepresentable`, `filter_dropped_by_upc`, `invalid_upc`.

## Concrete examples
- 2 lb carrots becomes `name="carrots"`, `line_item_measurements=[{quantity: 2, unit: "pound"}]` (or the supported spelling).
- 3 sweet potatoes becomes `quantity 3, unit "each"`.
- A plan-level hard constraint "no peanut products" has no health filter. The result carries `hard_constraint_unrepresentable`, and the handoff needs explicit review rather than sending it as a soft preference.
- Organic milk with a verified UPC: the UPC is sent, the ORGANIC filter would be ignored, so the result records `filter_dropped_by_upc` and shows it to the user.

## Constraints
- Never invent product IDs or UPCs; send a UPC only when it's a verified household fact.
- Never weaken a hard constraint into a preference or a filter Instacart may ignore.
- Pure function: deterministic for the same plan version; no I/O.
- Consumes the retailer-neutral plan and preference types; Instacart types stay inside the adapter.

## Dependencies
#146, #143, #145, #133 (canonical items, for stable names and verified UPCs).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each example above is a test.
- [ ] Every issue kind has a test that produces it.
- [ ] The same plan version always yields a byte-identical request body.
- [ ] Any `hard_constraint_unrepresentable` blocks confirmation until the user acknowledges it.

## Testing requirements
Table-driven unit tests plus a property test that translation never drops a plan line silently (each line maps to a line item or an issue).

## Out of scope
Calling Instacart, product search, choosing a retailer.

## Documentation requirements
Document the unit map and the issue kinds in the adapter README section.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
